body.heading: Gather your leaves
paragraphs: Collect fallen leaves in as many colours as you can find — red, gold, orange, brown, and maybe a green one that fell early.
In autumn, leaves stop making their green colour. The colours that were hiding underneath — yellows and oranges — finally get to show.

body.heading: Sort them out
paragraphs: Sort your leaves into piles. You could sort by colour, by size, or by shape. Each way of sorting tells a different story about your collection.
Count the leaves in each pile. Which pile is biggest? A collection sorted and counted is the start of real science.

body.heading: Press a favourite
paragraphs: Lay your favourite leaf flat between two sheets of paper, then stack heavy books on top. Leave it for a week.
When you open the books, your leaf will be flat and dry, ready to stick into a notebook. Pressed leaves can keep their colours for a long, long time.

takeaway: Sorting leaves by colour, size, or shape turns a walk into science, and pressing keeps one leaf forever.
safetyNotes: Only collect leaves already on the ground. Wash your hands after handling leaves, and never eat wild leaves or berries.
screenFreeExtension: Make a leaf parade on the floor, sorted by colour from lightest to darkest.
